children.name: Indicator
children.description: Drably plumaged birds with a remarkable behavioural adaptation — they guide humans and honey badgers to bee nests, then feed on the exposed wax and larvae after the nest is broken open. True to their scientific name, they are living indicators of wild bee colonies. They are brood parasites, laying their eggs in the nests of barbets, woodpeckers, and other cavity-nesting birds.

children.name: Indicator indicator
children.description: The greater honeyguide (Indicator indicator) is a bird in the family Indicatoridae, paleotropical near passerine birds related to the woodpeckers.

children.name: Indicator minor
children.description: The lesser honeyguide (Indicator minor) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae that is widely distributed across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Indicator variegatus
children.description: The scaly-throated honeyguide (Indicator variegatus) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. They have a mutualistic relationship with humans in which they attract beekeepers towards bees' nests and then feeding on the remains, especially larvae.

children.name: Indicator exilis
children.description: The least honeyguide (Indicator exilis) is a small species of bird in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Indicator willcocksi
children.description: Willcocks's honeyguide (Indicator willcocksi) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. It is found mainly throughout the African tropical rainforest. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the General Sir James Willcocks.

children.name: Indicator meliphilus
children.description: The pallid honeyguide (Indicator meliphilus) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Indicator conirostris
children.description: The lesser honeyguide (Indicator minor) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae that is widely distributed across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Indicator maculatus
children.description: The spotted honeyguide (Indicator maculatus) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Indicator pumilio
children.description: The dwarf honeyguide (Indicator pumilio) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Indicator archipelagicus
children.description: The Malaysian honeyguide (Indicator archipelagicus) is a bird in the family Indicatoridae, which are paleotropical near passerine birds related to the woodpeckers.

children.name: Indicator xanthonotus
children.description: The yellow-rumped honeyguide (Indicator xanthonotus) is a sparrow-sized bird in the honeyguide family that is found in Asia, mainly in montane forests along the Himalayas. They are very finch-like but the feet are strong and zygodactyl, with two toes facing forward and two backward. They perch on honeycombs and feed on wax. Males tend to be territorial and stay near honeycombs while females and juveniles forage widely. They are brood parasites, laying their eggs in the nests of tree-hole breeders, possibly barbets.

children.name: Melichneutes
children.description: Melichneutes — a genus of honeyguides in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Melichneutes robustus
children.description:
The lyre-tailed honeyguide (Melichneutes robustus) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. It is monotypic within the genus Melichneutes. It is found in the African tropical rainforest
Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Nigeria, Uganda and west of the Dahomey Gap in Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast and Ghana.

children.name: Melignomon
children.description: Melignomon — a genus of honeyguides in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Melignomon zenkeri
children.description:
Zenker's honeyguide (Melignomon zenkeri) is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. It is found in Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and Uganda.
The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German botanist Georg Zenker.

children.name: Prodotiscus
children.description: Small, slender honeyguides with a fine, sharply pointed bill that resembles a sunbird's more than a typical honeyguide's. They are the least known and most poorly studied of the honeyguides, with a preference for forest and woodland habitats.

children.name: Prodotiscus insignis
children.description: Cassin's honeybird (Prodotiscus insignis), also known as Cassin's honeyguide, is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae.

children.name: Prodotiscus regulorus
children.description: A honeyguide from southern Africa.

children.name: Prodotiscus regulus
children.description: The brown-backed honeybird (Prodotiscus regulus), also known as Wahlberg's honeybird, Wahlberg's honeyguide and sharp-billed honeyguide, is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. This bird is named after the Swedish naturalist Johan August Wahlberg.

children.name: Prodotiscus zambesiae
children.description: The green-backed honeybird (Prodotiscus zambesiae), also known as the eastern green-backed honeyguide, green-backed honeyguide and slender-billed honeyguide, is a species of bird in the family Indicatoridae. It is a nest parasite of three white-eye species. It is an insectivore that sometimes eats the waxy shed of scaly insects.
